findings.title: BuildIndex no longer single-flights per key
findings.body: BuildIndex used to hold cacheMu for the whole build, which also blocked GetIndex and serialized builders. The lock is now taken only to publish b.cache[key]. getOrCreateIndex is still check-then-act (GetIndex, and on nil call build/BuildIndex) and has no per-key lock or singleflight. Concurrent first searches, watch events, or init workers for the same NamespacedResource therefore build two bleve indexes. The later cache write blindly overwrites the earlier one, so one caller keeps writing and searching an index that is no longer in the cache while everyone else uses the other. The discarded index is never closed (memory and file-handle leak). For file indexes both builders use the same directory, so the second bleve.New fails and that caller gets an error even if the first build succeeded.

findings.title: File indexes cannot be reopened, so eager init crash-loops
findings.body: When size exceeds FileThreshold, BuildIndex always calls bleve.New on a stable path (Root/namespace/resource.group) and never bleve.Open. bleve.New fails if that directory already exists. A successful build, a killed process, or a failed init that already created the directory leaves the path on disk. Init now runs inside NewResourceServer and any BuildIndex error aborts server construction, so the next start hits the same bleve.New error and the process cannot boot until the directory is deleted by hand. The removed log was the only hint that an existing index/RV should be reused; the TODO remains unimplemented.

findings.title: Index init workers race on shared err
findings.body: searchSupport.init starts initWorkers goroutines that all do `_, _, err = s.build(...)` and `return err`, plus `totalBatchesIndexed++`, on variables owned by the outer function with no mutex or atomic. That is a data race. One worker can return another worker's nil and hide a failed namespace build, so startup continues after an index failed (the opposite of the comment that any init failure must block startup), or a success can be overwritten and fail startup incorrectly. The span attribute namespaced_indexed is also racy. This function is now on the blocking startup path.

findings.title: Postgres storage-server startup test is skipped
findings.body: TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer is the integration coverage for the storage-server target coming up and serving /metrics. This change makes NewResourceServer run unified-storage Init (stats, index build, watch) during that startup, which this test previously never reached because it never issued a storage RPC. The PR skips the test on postgres with a TODO that it fails in Drone, so the CI job that would catch a postgres-specific eager-init failure no longer runs it.
